claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child. My son Alex is 17, and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, I need to understand his current circumstances. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex still in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college anymore. He finished his education and isn't doing any training programs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**Is Alex currently working? And if so, does he work 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Let me ask another important question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to get a complete picture:

**Does Alex live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or are you looking to make a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm looking to make a new claim. I haven't been receiving Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, the other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For young people aged 16-19 (like Alex, who is 17), you can continue to receive Child Benefit **only if** they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex has finished his education and is not currently in any training program, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit, even though he:
- Lives with you
- Is not working 24 hours or more per week
- Is not claiming benefits in his own right

**If Alex's circumstances change** - for example, if he decides to return to education, start college, or begin an approved training program - you may be able to claim Child Benefit for him at that time. In that case, you would need to make a new claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
